ACT-J08
ENGLISH TEST
PASSAGE I
Seeing Streams in a New Light
As cities grew, in the nineteenth, and twentieth
centuries, thousands of urban streams were diverted
underground into large metal or concrete pipes called
culverts. Culverting controlled the paths of urban
waterways and created space for new construction, but
its unintended consequences—increased flooding, habitat
loss, maintenance costs—far outweigh its benefits today.
To alleviate these issues, communities should invest in
“daylighting” long-buried waterways by uncovering and
then restoring them to more natural conditions. [
